method: BASELINE. scope: In: ss 4 (spouse), 5, 6, 6A; ss 18, 19, 21-29 (jurisdiction to hold an inquest, with s 24(2) notice of legal representation; dispensing, with s 25(3); inquests required); s 35 (duty to report); s 38 (death certificates); ss 54, 56, 57, 60, 61(7), 65; s 75 (self-inflicted deaths); ss 79, 81, 83(2)-(7) (resumption, findings, fresh inquests); ss 84-87 (Supreme Court, with the s 87(1) 21 days to serve the order); ss 89(6), 90(4)-(6), 91, 94, 95-99 (post mortems, whole organs, exhumation, protection, objections); ss 100-101 (disposal of remains); the maximum penalties of the offences an individual can commit in the Chapters encoded, with s 44 (ss 35, 44, 53, 62, 74, 75, 76, 100, 103A; not s 101M, Chapter 9A being out). Out: Chapter 2 (coronial officers), Part 3.3 (fires and explosions), Chapter 5 (investigation scenes, except the s 44 penalty), the procedure and witness-compulsion sections, Chapter 9A (Domestic Violence Death Review Team), Chapter 10 machinery, Schedules 1-3. The Coroners Regulation is not deposited: what it prescribes is asked. Reasons in NOTES.md.
